high.title: Fed Chair Considers Major Changes, Markets Get Even Fewer Clues on Interest Rates
high.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is reportedly proposing to reduce the number of FOMC meetings per year — currently held 8 times annually — a structural shift that would represent a significant overhaul of U.S. monetary policy communication. At the July 30th FOMC meeting, the committee voted 9-3 to hold rates steady, a decision largely anticipated by markets. However, investor sentiment turned negative as Warsh declined to provide detailed reasoning for the hold or clarify whether he would support rate hikes should inflation fail to moderate further. Since taking the Fed Chair role in May, Warsh has signaled a more opaque communication style, leaving markets with fewer forward guidance anchors.

high.title: SBV Raises State Treasury Deposit Exclusion Ratio in LDR Calculation to 50%, Effective 1 August
high.summary: On 30 July 2026, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) issued Decision No. 1743/QĐ-NHNN, raising the deduction ratio applied to State Treasury term deposits when calculating the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) from its previous level to **50%**. The measure takes effect from **1 August 2026 through 31 July 2028**, under the framework of Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular 25/2026/TT-NHNN.

medium.title: Weekly Stock Market Review: TAL and FRT Shares Unexpectedly Hit Upper Limits, PNJ Touches 6-Year Low
medium.summary:
The VN-Index closed the final trading session of the week (July 31) with a notable reversal — after gaining over 13 points in the morning session, aggressive profit-taking in the afternoon erased all gains, with the index falling nearly 9 points by close as selling pressure dominated. TAL (Taseco Real Estate Investment JSC) and FRT were standout performers, both hitting their daily upper price limits with no sellers, driven by TAL's Q2/2026 earnings surge of over 320% year-on-year. However, PNJ (Phu Nhuan Jewelry) touched a 6-year price low, reflecting broader market weakness. The afternoon sell-off pattern suggests fragile market sentiment and limited conviction among domestic retail buyers despite pockets of strong individual stock performance. For equity-focused fund managers, the VN-Index's inability to hold intraday gains signals continued caution; liquidity bifurcation between surging individual stocks and broad index weakness warrants close monitoring of overall market direction.

medium.title: New Ranking: Top 10 Most Profitable Banks in Vietnam – H1 2026
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking sector posted aggregate pre-tax profit of approximately VND 223.7 trillion in H1 2026, a robust ~21% year-on-year increase from VND 184.8 trillion in H1 2025. Profit concentration is intensifying: the Top 10 banks — Vietcombank, VietinBank, MB, BIDV, VPBank, Techcombank, Agribank, HDBank, ACB, and SHB — collectively earned VND 183.1 trillion, up 29.1% YoY, now commanding ~82% of total sector profit versus ~77% a year ago. Smaller and mid-tier banks, by contrast, saw profits decline sharply, with some down more than 70% YoY. For bond and equity investors, the strong earnings momentum at the systemically important banks (SOCBs + large private banks) supports sector credit quality and reduces NPL-related systemic risk — a modest positive for Vietnamese sovereign and bank bond spreads. The widening profitability gap between large and small banks may also accelerate consolidation dynamics, which the SBV has been encouraging. Watch for whether higher bank profits translate into improved capital adequacy ratios and reduced pressure on the SBV to provide liquidity support.

medium.title: Full H1 2026 Profit Overview: Vietcombank Posts 58% Q2 Profit Surge; MB Up 41%
medium.summary: Vietcombank — Vietnam's largest listed bank and a key FX market participant — recorded Q2 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 17.4 trillion, up a striking 57.9% YoY, with net interest income rising 35.2%. Total assets reached VND 2.66 quadrillion, up 8.8% YTD, while customer loans grew 5.1% and deposits 3.4%. MB delivered Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 10.6 trillion (+40.7% YoY), with H1 cumulative profit of VND 20.2 trillion (+27.1%), securing a Top 3 sector ranking. The strong NIM expansion at Vietcombank is particularly noteworthy for FX and rates watchers: as the dominant state-owned commercial bank and the SBV's primary conduit for FX intervention, Vietcombank's balance sheet health and liquidity position directly influence USD/VND market depth and interbank dynamics. Robust deposit growth across SOCBs also suggests system liquidity remains ample, limiting upward pressure on interbank VND rates near-term.

medium.title: Major Banks — Vietcombank, VietinBank, Agribank — to Suspend All Transactions for Accounts Failing Biometric/ID Update Requirements
medium.summary: Under SBV Circulars 17/2024/TT-NHNN and 18/2024/TT-NHNN, Vietnam's largest banks — including Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, Agribank, MB, and VPBank — are now enforcing a full transaction freeze on accounts that have not completed mandatory identity document and biometric data updates. Affected transaction types span counter services (cash withdrawals, transfers), digital banking (app/web transfers, bill payments, e-wallet top-ups), and ATM/POS operations. The SBV's stated objective is to strengthen payment security and enforce account ownership verification. While primarily a consumer compliance matter, the policy has broader market relevance: forced account freezes at scale across systemically important banks could temporarily disrupt retail payment flows and, at the margin, reduce overnight VND liquidity velocity in the interbank market. International fund managers should monitor whether enforcement creates any short-term friction in capital repatriation or settlement for foreign investors operating through local custodian accounts.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of 30 July: Market Stabilizes with ACB Leading at 7.8% for 12-Month Tenor
medium.summary: As of 30 July, the deposit rate landscape showed broad stability with no new adjustments recorded. ACB continues to lead the market at **7.8% p.a. for 12-month deposits**, followed by Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%). Seven banks now offer 7.0% or above for the 12-month tenor. The Big 4 state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) maintain a uniform rate of **6.8% p.a. for 12- and 18-month tenors** and 6.6% for 6- and 9-month tenors. The rate environment suggests the market has absorbed prior localized adjustments, with no fresh upward pressure evident — a signal that system liquidity remains relatively comfortable heading into August.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of 31 July: Rates Hold Steady on Final Day of July
medium.summary: On the last day of July, listed deposit rates across Vietnamese banks showed virtually no change, confirming the stabilization trend. ACB retained its market-leading position at **7.8% for 12 months**, with the same ranking order as the prior day. The Big 4 bloc continues offering 6.8% at the 12-month benchmark. The persistence of elevated rates at smaller and mid-sized banks relative to the state-owned bloc suggests a bifurcated funding environment — private banks are paying a meaningful premium (up to 100bps over Big 4) to attract retail deposits, which warrants monitoring for any signs of funding stress if credit demand accelerates post the LDR rule change.
